text:
ava: overnight autoscaler removed 2 preemptible GPU nodes in us-west2 (~02:14) and a couple of training pods got stuck. drain returned 'cannot evict pod: would violate PodDisruptionBudget' and CA aborted. nodes still terminated by cloud provider after cordon timeout. anyone see the same behavior?

ben: saw it too. CA logs: "scaleDown: node cordoned, drain failed: PDB violation". CA doesn't force PDB patches so it aborted and we lost some in-progress checkpoints when preemptible window closed. :grimacing:

lucas: quick summary of options we have (tradeoffs):
- mark nondurable workers as safe-to-evict: annotation cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict=true (fast, low risk for idempotent workloads)
- convert PDBs from minAvailable to maxUnavailable where sensible (makes evictions possible without complex operator)
- introduce a temporary operator that can relax PDBs after a graceful timeout when autoscaler is stuck (more invasive)
- extend termination window with node-termination-handler so checkpointers get time to finish (better UX, increases cost)

iris: worth noting: some pods are truly critical (checkpoint-writer) and we should protect them with a high-priority PriorityClass so preemption doesn't kill them mid-checkpoint. priorityClass won't stop scale-down though — it just affects preemption order.

ava: proposal for a low-risk rollout:
1) Identify candidate deployments (batch workers, retryable trainers) and set annotation safe-to-evict=true in their Helm charts.
2) Change pod-deletion-cost on stateful checkpointers to a high positive value so CA prefers other pods for eviction.
3) Add a small controller (drain-fallback) that watches CA drain failures: if node drain fails and the node is preemptible, after N seconds it will patch only the PDBs referencing those pods to temporarily allow eviction (patch minAvailable->0 or convert to maxUnavailable=1), then requeue the drain. Controller must record audit and revert patches immediately after scale-down.

ben: controller sounds risky but pragmatic for preemptible pools. alternative simpler path is to reduce PDB strictness for anything that has >1 replica and is restartable. we should compute how many replicas would be impacted.

lucas: CA already uses pod-deletion-cost and safe-to-evict annotations. Example: set annotation in Helm values for workers:

  metadata:
    annotations:
      cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "true"
      controller.kubernetes.io/pod-deletion-cost: "0"

And for checkpointers, in values.yaml set deletion cost higher: 
  metadata:
    annotations:
      controller.kubernetes.io/pod-deletion-cost: "100"

This nudges CA without touching PDBs.

iris: sample PDB change (convert to maxUnavailable):

apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: trainer-pdb
spec:
  maxUnavailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: trainer

Or temporary patch to relax: 

kubectl patch pdb trainer-pdb -p '{"spec":{"minAvailable":0}}'

Note: patching live PDBs needs strict audit and quick revert.

ava: node-termination-handler idea: for preemptible-gpu node-pool we can increase the graceful shutdown delay from 30s to 5m to give checkpointers time to flush. That will increase cost (longer preemptible occupancy) but reduce lost work. Ops decision needed.

ben: I'll run a simulation in staging tonight: create a preemptible pool, deploy mix of checkpointers + workers, set annotations, and trigger CA scale-down to observe behavior.

lucas: I'll add safe-to-evict to batch-worker chart and add documentation about pod-deletion-cost semantics in the charts repo.

iris: I'll produce a one-page audit of all PDBs in prod across GPU pools and flag ones with minAvailable >0 for single-replica sets. probably 6-8 candidates.

sre-bot: deployment-alert: staging-sim (preemptible-test) will run at 22:00 UTC per @ben.

ava: action items:
- ben: staging sim + report (tonight)
- lucas: chart changes (safe-to-evict & deletion-cost) PR this week
- iris: PDB audit and risk matrix by EOD tomorrow
- ava: prototype drain-fallback operator design doc (POC not to be rolled to prod) next week

ava: long-term we should consider autoscaler knob that can escalate after X failed drains (e.g., 'force-evict-after') but that doesn't exist upstream. Patching PDBs is the pragmatic in-cluster way. Keep the change scoped to preemptible GPU nodepools only. :thumbsup:

ben: noted. will include metrics to detect when CA aborted drains due to PDBs and alert ops so we don't silently lose work. :eyes:

lucas: +1, and we should tie cost analysis to each option: longer termination window means extra minutes billed; CA PDB relax means less rework. I'll draft a short cost/benefit table for the PR.

ava: OK — thanks team. we'll reconvene after the staging sim.
